 Commonjudgment
 These two claim petitions are filed by the respective
petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
against the common respondents, claiming compensation
with respect to the injuries sustained by petitioner in
Mvc 5018/2023 and death of deceased Brijesh @ V.
Rijesh in Mvc No.5019/2023 in a road traffic accident. 
 2 .  The above said petitions arose out of the same accident and the respondents in the said petitions are same. Hence, the above two petitions were clubbed and common evidence was recorded in MVC.5018/2023 and hence the petitions are taken to pass common judgment. 
 3. The brief facts of the petition averments are that; On 09-05-2023 at about 7-00 p.m., the petitioner Ajith in MVC No.5018/2023 as a pillion rider and the deceased Brijesh @ Vrijesh in MVC No.5019/2023 as rider were proceeding in a two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-05-JV-0533 from Guttahalli towards Rayasandra and when they reached near SJR Fine Grow apartment, Rayasandra Guttahalli road, Rayasandra,
Guddi vs Hasan S on 2 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17303822/
2 Bangalore, at that time the driver of the Auto bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AH-7090 came from opposite direction in  SCCH-24 4 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023 rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioners motorcycle, result of which the pillion rider and rider of the said vehicle sustained severe injuries and rider succumbed to the injuries.
 3(a). Soon after the accident the petitioner in MVC.5018/2023 was taken to Nimhans Hospital wherein admitted as an inpatient for about 7 days. So far the petitioner has spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical and conveyance expenses. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and health. The petitioner was doing carpenter work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month . Due to the injuries sustained, he became disabled and he cannot do his normal work as before. 
 3(b) It is stated in MVC.5019/2023 that deceased Brijesh @ V Rijesh was aged about 19 years, he was hale and healthy prior to the accident. The deceased was doing carpenter work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month. The petitioners have spent for Rs.1,00,000/-
towards funeral expenses. The petitioners are totally depending on the income of the deceased. 
 SCCH-24 5 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023  4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 - the R.C. owner of Auto bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AH-7090 has remained absent and hence he was placed ex-parte. 
 5. The respondent No.2/ the Insurer of Auto bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AH-7090 have filed written statement in both cases and admitted the coverage of policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy. It is contended that there was no negligence on the part of the insured vehicle. It is contended that the above petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties as the alleged accident was caused due to the carelessness act of the deceased. It is contended that the deceased who was the rider of the said scooter had no valid driving license and the said scooter was no valid insurance policy and the driver of insured auto was also not holding valid and effective Guddi vs Hasan S on 2 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17303822/
3 driving license and the said vehicle had no valid RC and FC as on the date of accident.
 6. On the basis of rival pleadings following common issues have been framed;
 Issue in MVC 5018/2023  1. Whether the petitioners prove that he  has sustained grievous injuries on the  SCCH-24 6 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023  account of the road traffic accident on 9-  05-2023 at about 07-00 p.m. near SJR  Fine Grow Apartment, Rayasandra  Gattahalli Road, Rayasandra, Bengaluru  City, due to rash and negligent driving of  the driver of Auto bearing Reg.no.KA-01-  AH-7090? 
 2. Whether the petitioners are entitled  for Compensation? If so, what is the  quantum and from whom?
 3. What order or award? 
 Issue in MVC 5019/2023  1. Whether the petitioners prove that,
 Sri.Brijesh @ Vrijesh died on account of  road traffic accident n 9-05-2023 at  about 07-00 p.m. near SJR Fine Grow  Apartment, Rayasandra Gattahalli Road,
 Rayasandra, Bengaluru City, due to rash  and negligent driving of the driver of Auto  bearing Reg.no.KA-01-AH-7090?
 2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for  compensation as claimed? If so, what is  the quantum? From whom Payable? 
 3. What order or award? 
 7. Common evidence was recorded in MVC.5018/2023. 
In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.2 in MVC 5019/2023 got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked document as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8, Ex.P12. The  SCCH-24 7 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023 Guddi vs Hasan S on 2 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17303822/
4 petitioner in MVC 5018/2023 has examined himself as PW.2 and two witnesses are examined as PW.3 and PW.4 and got marked documents as Ex.P.9, P10, and P13 to Ex.P20. The respondent no.1 has examined its Senior Manager as RW.1 and got marked insurance policy as Ex.R1. 
 8. I have heard the arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and the respondent no.2 in both the petitions and perused the entire materials placed on record. 
 9. My findings on the above issues in MVC 5018/2023 are as follows;
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative  Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3: As per final order,
 for the following; 
 10. My findings on the above issues in MVC 5019/2023 are as follows;
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative  Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3: As per final order,
 for the following;
 SCCH-24 8 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023  REASONS  11. Issue No.1 in M.V.C.NO.5018/2023 and Issue no.1 in M.V.C.No.5019/2023:- As these issues are interconnected they are taken up together for common discussion to avoid repetition of facts. 
 12. In order to substantiate that the accident in question has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Auto bearing No.KA-01-AH-7090 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) the petitioner no.2 in MVC No.5019/2023 has got examined himself as PW.1 and the petitioner in MVC No.5018/2023 has got examined himself as PW.2. The PWs.1 and 2 have specifically deposed in their examination in chief that the driver of offending vehicle drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle in which PW.2 and deceased were proceeding, result of which PW.2 sustained injuries and deceased succumbed to the injuries. 
Guddi vs Hasan S on 2 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17303822/
5  13. In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 and PW.2 have relied upon Ex.P1 to P7 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, spot  SCCH-24 9 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023 mahazar, sketch, IMV report, Inquest mahazar, PM report, charge sheet.
 14. On the basis of the complaint lodged by Ravindra Paswan, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No 0166/2023 of Electronic City Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 338, 304-A of IPC and u/Sec. 134 (a&b), 187 of MV Act. The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279, 338, 304-A of IPC and u/Sec. 134 (a& b), 3(1), 181,
5, 180 of MV Act.
 15. It is vehemently argued by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 that the accident in question has occurred in the middle of the road, on account of which the front portion of both the vehicles have got damaged and that at the time of accident, the rider of motorcycle i.e., deceased was not holding driving licence and both the deceased and injured who were traveling in the motorcycle were not in head gear hence the rider of motorcycle has also contributed negligence.
 SCCH-24 10 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023  16. In the light of the argument canvassed by the learned counsel for respondent no.2, if the materials placed on record is perused, nowhere in the police records there is any mention about the rider of motorcycle not holding driving license or that they were not wearing helmet. If really the deceased was not having valid driving license and if really they were not wearing helmet then investigation officer would have filed charge sheet against the deceased and injured under MV Act, but charge sheet is filed only against the driver of offending vehicle but not against the deceased and injured. It is true that in the medical records right mark was put before the column no helmet but the medical officer or the concerned staffs of Guddi vs Hasan S on 2 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17303822/
6 the hospital authority are not the competent person to state whether deceased and injured at the time of accident were in the helmet or not. Even if it is taken for a while for the sake of discussion that at the time of accident the deceased was not holding driving license and they were not wearing helmet then also that would be no ground to attribute negligence against the rider of the motorcycle. 
 17. In K. Anusha and Others Vs. Regional Manager,
Sriram General Insurance Company Limited, it was observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that "To establish  SCCH-24 11 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023 contributory negligence, some act or omission, which materially contributed to the accident or the damage,
should be attributed to the person against whom it is alleged". In the said case, reference was made of Judgment in Pramodkumar Rasikbhai Jhaveri Vs.
Karmasey Kunvargi Tak and Others wherein it was observed that "to hold that where by his negligence, one party places another in a situation of danger, which compels that other to act quickly in order to extricate himself, it does not amount to contributory negligence, if that other acts in a way which, with the benefit of hindsight is shown not to have been the best way out of the difficulty".
 18. In Swadling Vs. Cooper wherein it was observed that "the mere failure to avoid the collision by taking some extraordinary precaution, does not in itself constitute negligence". 
 19. In 2009 Supreme (SC) 995 between Raj Rani &
Ors, Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.Ld., & Ors., it was observed that "The question of contributory negligence arises when there has been some act or omission on the claimants part, which has materially contributed to the damage caused and is of such a nature that it may  SCCH-24 12 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023 properly be described as 'negligence'. Negligence ordinarily means breach of a legal duty to care, but when used in the expression "contributory negligence", it does not mean breach of any duty. It only means the failure by a person to use reasonable care for the safety of either Guddi vs Hasan S on 2 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17303822/
7 himself or his property, so that he becomes blameworthy in part as an author of his own wrong".
 20. If the observation made in the aforesaid rulings it can be said that not holding driving license by the victim and not wearing helmet etc are not the ground to say that victim too has contributed negligence. 
 21. If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, at the time of accident the deceased and PW.2 was proceeding in the motorcycle from Guttahalli towards Rayasandra. The offending vehicle which came from opposite direction hit to the motor cycle. It is two way road. The centre of the road is marked in the sketch with lines. The accident in question has occurred on the left side of Guttahalli -Rayasandra road. The driver of the Auto Rickshaw by crossing the center mark took his vehicle towards right and hit against the motorcycle. 
Hence, from the spot mahazar and sketch it can be said that the driver of offending vehicle is the sole cause for  SCCH-24 13 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023 accident. Hence, without discussing much on this point,
this court holds issue no.1 in MVC No.5018/2023 and in MVC No.5019/2023 in the affirmative. 
 22. Issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.5018/2023: P.W.2 has given evidence to the effect of his sustained severe injuries. Petitioner has produced abundant medical documents. As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents which are at Ex.P.9 and Ex.P13. On going through the medical records it reveals that soon after the accident petitioner has taken treatment at NIMHANS Hospital, Bangalore, wherein admitted as an inpatient from 12-05-2023 to 13-05-2023 for a period of 2 days. As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained two injuries which are grievous in nature. 
 23. Dr. Shailesh A V Rao -Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon at Padmashree Diagnostics, Bengaluru has given evidence as Pw3 and through him OPD record,
skull X-report, Neuro Psychological report, mini mental state examination report are got marked as Ex.P.15 to Ex.P.18. P.W.3 has deposed that petitioner consulted him at Padmashree Diagnostics, Bangalore on 29-03- 2024 and on 02-04-2024 for the assessment of disability. 
Guddi vs Hasan S on 2 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17303822/
8 PW.3 further deposed that the neuro psychological  SCCH-24 14 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023 Assessment of petitioner was done, his IQ was 78 (90- 109). He is below average in thinking and reasoning and has moderate mental retardation. On IDEAS, he obtained a score 06, indicating moderate disability of 40%. His MMSE score is 22-30 which low score is. PW.3 further deposed that he has assessed the disability as per the disability Assessment and Certification Guidelines issued by DGHS, GOI during 2001 and 2018. On the modified Rankin Scale, the petitioner has score of 1. As per the guidelines, this amounts to a disability of around 15%. 
 24. If the cross examination of PW.3 is perused,
admittedly he is not a treated doctor. 
 25. If the evidence of PW.2 who is an injured is perused,
during the cross examination he has given rational answer to all the questions posed to him without any hindrance even for a while and cleverly has given answer to the entire question posed to him and it is he who himself has represented the case without his being represented through guardian. Now at this juncture it would be relevant to refer here the judgment rendered in MFA No.9065/2019 c/w MFA No.3748/2019 between Raghugowda Vs. The Mangaing Director, BMTC, wherein,
in the similar set of facts the doctor has reported that  SCCH-24 15 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023 petitioner has sustained 50% disability but the court while observing that the petitioner has filed application on his own and as a normal person he has prosecuted the petition, he has given evidence on his own and he is a normal person with normal intellect has observed that petitioner has not suffered any disability and only with a view to get higher compensation, he has chosen to produce a false report and PW.3 being a responsible doctor has not only given a false report but also given evidence on oath based on such false report has decline to consider the percentage of disability allegedly suffered by the petitioner. 
 26. The observation made in the aforesaid ruling is Guddi vs Hasan S on 2 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17303822/
9 aptly applicable to the case in hand. Hence, this court declines to consider the evidence of PW.3 and intern declines to consider the neurological disability assessed by the PW.3. When petitioner has sustained head injury and underwent surgery, under such circumstances because of the head injury suffered by him it may have caused some amount of loss of amenities and discomfort. Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort but not under the head loss of future income. 
 SCCH-24 16 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023  27. Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads. 
 28. Towards pain and sufferings, the petitioner shown to have sustained two grievous injuries. Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment etc it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.60,000/- towards pain and suffering. 
 29. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, the petitioner has produced medical bills for Rs.73,487/- as per Ex.P14 As such petitioner is entitled for Rs.73,487/- under the head medical expenses.
 30. Further for 2 days of hospitalization at Nimhans Hospital, Bangalore and for his taking follow up treatment in the said hospitals, requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment, for follow-ups has incurred traveling expenses, he has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other  SCCH-24 17 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023 incidental expenses therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.15,000/-. 
 31 . It is submitted by the petitioner that he was doing carpenter work and earning sum of Rs.20,000/- per month. But to substantiate the said contention petitioner has not produced any materials. Hence this court Guddi vs Hasan S on 2 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17303822/
10 considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.15,500/- p.m.
 32. The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and taken treatment for 2 days as inpatient. Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of two months as complete laid down period. Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period for two month. 
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.31,000/-
towards loss of income during the laid down period. 
 33. The petitioner at his age of 38 years has suffered grievous injuries. Hence taking in to consideration the said aspect the petitioner is entitled for  SCCH-24 18 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023 sum of Rs.75,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomforts. 
Sl. Heads Amount No.
1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs.60,000/-
2. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs.15,000/-
 charges and nourishing food 3. Medical expenses Rs.73,487/-
4. Loss of income during laid down Rs.31,000/-
 period 5. Loss of discomfort and amenities Rs.75,000/-
 Total Rs.2,54,487/-
Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,54,487/- ( Rupees Two Lakh Fifty Four Thousand Four Hundred Eighty Seven only). 
 34. ISSUE NO.2 in MVC No.5019/2023:- PW.1 is the father of deceased. It is the contention of the petitioners that they being the parents, minor brother and sister are entirely depending on the earnings of the deceased and that deceased was doing carpenter work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
 35. After considering the materials placed on Guddi vs Hasan S on 2 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17303822/
11 record and the submission made by the learned respective counsels, it is not in serious dispute that deceased was died in the road traffic accident. It is stated  SCCH-24 19 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023 by the petitioners that at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 19 years. In this regard, the petitioners have produced Aadhaar card and SSLC marks card of the deceased at Ex.P11 and Ex.P12 which shows his date of birth as 01-05-2005 and as the accident took place in the year 2023. Therefore, the deceased has completed 18 years as on the date of accident. 
 36 As it is observed earlier, it is contended by the petitioners that deceased was doing carpenter work and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. admittedly there is no documents placed to prove the income of the deceased. 
When there are no materials to prove the income of the deceased, court has to take notional income of the deceased to assess the quantum of compensation under different heads. 
 37. So far as the avocation and income of the deceased, in order to prove the same petitioners have not produced any materials. Hence taking in to consideration the age of the deceased and the year in which accident in question had occurred, this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/- p.m.
 38. Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, 
 SCCH-24 20 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023 considering the family status of the deceased as he was bachelor 50% of annual income is to be deducted towards the personal expenses and remaining 50% is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.
 39 . Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors/Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd) it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death. It is further observed that in case the Guddi vs Hasan S on 2 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17303822/
12 deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40% of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation. 
Hence in the instant case as the victim was 18 years the addition towards future prospect should be 40%.
 SCCH-24 21 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023  40. Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/- of which 40% is added towards the future prospect which comes to Rs.21,700/-. Out of it if 50% is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.10,850/-. The appropriate multiplier applicable is 18 for the age of the deceased. Accordingly the petitioner is entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.23,43,600/- (10,850x 12 x 18). 
 41. Because of the untimely death of deceased the petitioner's no1 and 2 have lost their son and petitioner no.3 and 4 have lost their brother thereby lost the love and affection of deceased. So far as the quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157. In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/,
Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively. It is further observed that the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years. The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017. 
 SCCH-24 22 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023  42. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd., The Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife, parental consortium and filial consortium. This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors. 
By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should Guddi vs Hasan S on 2 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17303822/
13 be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-. Hence,
this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium. Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/-. 
 43 . In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
 SL Heads Amount  1 Transportation and Rs. 18,150/-
 Funeral Expenses  2 Loss of estate Rs. 18,150/-
 3 . Loss of parental Rs. 1,93,600/-
 consortium and filial  consortium  (Rs.48,400x4)
 SCCH-24 23 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023  4. Loss of Dependency Rs.23,43,600/-
 Total Rs.25,73,500/-
 Thus, in all petitioner is entitled to Rs.25,73,500/-
(Rupees Twenty Five Lakh Seventy Three Thousand Five Hundred only) and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case. 
 44. As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident. The learned counsel for respondent no.2 has disputed the liability of respondent no.2 on the ground that as on the date of accident the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid driving license to drive the nature of vehicle which he alleged to have been driven, hence submitted to exonerate the respondent no.2 from the liability of paying compensation. 
 45. While discussing issue no.1, this court has observed that Auto bearing No.KA-01-AH-7090 was involved in the accident.
 46. IN 2018(2) CC 101(SC) Jagadish Kumar Sood/United India Insurance Company Limited where in Guddi vs Hasan S on 2 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17303822/
14  SCCH-24 24 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023 it is held that Light Motor vehicle includes transport vehicle as per weight prescribed in section 2(21). License issued to drive light motor vehicle would cover transport vehicle within the prescribed weight and be valid. 
 47 . In ILR 2018 KAR 2094 Sri Yamanappa and Another/ Sri Suresh and Another 2018 (1) KCCR 689- Doddavenkataramanappa / Mallesh K and Another and 2018 (2) KCCR 1371- Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Ltd Kalaburagi / Shekhar Dandi and Others similar line of observation was made by holding that If a driver holding a driving licence to drive a light motor vehicle (Non transport ) and if he is not holding a driving license to drive a transport vehicle, he can drive the transport vehicle.
 48. In (2017) 14 SCC 663 between Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd. It was held that "A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7500 kg would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a roadroller, "Unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg. Further, holder of a driving license to drive class of "light motor vehicle" as provided in S.10(2) (d) is  SCCH-24 25 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023 competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7500 kg or a motor car or tractor or roadroller, the "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg". 
 49. On going through the above decision, it makes it clear that if a person is holding a license to drive a light motor vehicle registered for a private use who is driving similar vehicle which is registered or insured for the purpose of carrying passengers for hire or reward would not require an endorsement to drive a transport vehicle as the same is not contemplated by the provisions of the Act. 
It further made it clear that if a driver holding a driving licence to drive a light motor vehicle (non - transport ) and if he is not holding a driving license to drive a transport vehicle he can drive the transport vehicle. In the light of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court and on perusal Guddi vs Hasan S on 2 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17303822/
15 of the documents it clearly indicates that the driver was holding driving license to drive light motor vehicle (non transport) and same was in currency from as on the date of accident . Under such circumstances he is competent to drive a transport vehicle. When admittedly the policy was in force and the driver was holding driving license, the insurer cannot escape from the liability. Hence the respondent no.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle  SCCH-24 26 MVC 5018/2023  C/w 5019/2023 is liable to pay the compensation. The compensation shall carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit. Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
